title: Runtime hallmark selector + prefetch prober for arch-and-seqlen-aware kernel staging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current kernel-choice pipeline defaults to a small set of heuristics that do not account for transient load and the joint distribution of GPU architecture and sequence-length tails. As a result, certain mid-tail workloads (mixed short + long prefill) observe 25–40% higher p95 latency than expected.

Goal: Implement a lightweight "hallmark" fingerprinting selector that maps (GPU architecture, seqlen-bucket, runtime-load-signal, kv-cache-hit) -> ranked kernel candidate list, and a low-impact prefetch prober that continuously micro-benchmarks kernel latency for hot hallmark buckets. This should enable faster warm-starting of the best kernel for a request and safe automatic fallback when latency regressions are detected.

Approach:
- Hallmark fingerprint: compute concise runtime fingerprints per request type (gpu_model, sm_version, seqlen_bucket, kv_cache_flag, batch_shape_hint). Keep fingerprint size < 64 bytes and maintain an LRU store of recent fingerprints with aggregated latency and throughput statistics.
- Slot-based staging: maintain ordered candidate lists per hallmark with metadata (empiric p50/p95, cost score), and a slot for the active kernel and one or two safety candidates.
- Prefetch prober: run low-priority micro-probes on underutilized devices to measure candidate kernels across seqlen buckets. Probes are throttled and budget-capped per-node to avoid interfering with production traffic.
- Updating policy: prefer kernels that meet latency SLOs under current load and have a lower expected token-cost; degrade to safety kernel if p95 exceeds SLO over rolling window. Use exponential backoff before switching kernels under noisy signals.
- Telemetry: emit hallmark-id, kernel-choice, probe-latencies, and rolling p50/p95 into runtime telemetry. Add dashboard with hallmark heatmap and per-hallmark candidate ranking drift.

Why this differs from prior work: existing autotuners focus on offline profiling or seqlen histograms centralized per model. This ticket targets a compact, online fingerprinting layer that pairs ephemeral runtime load signals with architecture metadata to accelerate warm-start kernel selection without heavy global re-profiling.

Risks: noisy probes affecting SLAs; fingerprint cardinality blowup; slow convergence when workload drifts rapidly. Mitigations listed below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hallmark fingerprint implementation that produces stable keys for common request classes.
2) Per-hallmark candidate store persisted in memory with eviction and metadata (p50/p95/last_probe).
3) Prefetch prober that runs within a 0.5% CPU/GPU budget and collects representative latencies for at least 5 candidate kernels across at least 3 seqlen buckets.
4) Automatic kernel switcher that changes active kernel only after at least 3 consistent probe cycles and with exponential backoff; switches reduce observed p95 by >=10% on targeted hallmark test cases.
5) Telemetry dashboard showing hallmark heatmap and kernel ranking drift.
6) Safety fallback to reference kernel with a verified latency penalty < 2x and no functional differences.
7) Tests: unit tests for fingerprint canonicalization, integration canary in staging with synthetic mixed-length traffic, and e2e load test demonstrating no regression in other hallmarks.
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting notes: aligned with SLOs team on acceptable probe budget; agreed to cap prober to 0.5% device utilization and 1 probe per 10s per idle slot.

2026-02-19: Design review feedback from Priya (Runtime): prefer deterministic seqlen bucketing edges used across runtime to avoid drift; add a TTL of 12h on hallmark entries to prevent cardinality explosion.

2026-02-22: Prototype update: implemented fingerprint canonicalizer and LRU store. Early microbenchmark shows candidate metadata adds ~600B per hallmark in memory. Need to reduce per-entry overhead; exploring Bloom-filter encoded counters and lossy aggregation for infrequent hallmarks.

2026-02-25: Security/SRE sync: prober network egress restricted, probes must not call external endpoints; agreed to local microkernel invocation only. SRE requested opt-out flag for critical clusters.

2026-02-28: Performance trial in staging: enabled hallmark routing for 8 representative models. Observed p95 down 12% on mixed prefill workloads after warmstart window; probe overhead measured at 0.38% GPU cycles.
2026-03-01: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1248. Requesting product/metrics sign-off before canarying to 2 prod shards.
